record.paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
record.context_brief: Combinatorics of small tensegrity configuration spaces
record.original_question: Let B_d(G) = (R^d)^n be the configuration space of realizations P = (p_1, ..., p_n) of a graph G with n labeled vertices in R^d, and stratify B_d(G) by the equivalence classes of the self-stress spaces W(G, P) under sign-preserving homeomorphisms of fibers as in Definitions 1.2 and 1.3. Determine the combinatorial structure of the stratifications of B_2(K_6), B_3(K_4), and B_3(K_5), including the strata of all dimensions and the adjacency relations among those strata.

evidence.quote: Problem 1 Describe the combinatorics of B2(K6), B3(K4) and B3(K5).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite graph with vertex set {1, 2, ..., n} and edge set E(G). For an integer d ≥ 1, the configuration space of G in R^d is B_d(G) := (R^d)^n, whose points are realizations P = (p_1, ..., p_n) with p_i ∈ R^d.

For a realization P ∈ B_d(G), a self-stress on (G, P) is an assignment w : E(G) → R of weights w_{ij} to the edges {i,j} ∈ E(G) satisfying the equilibrium condition at every vertex i:
   sum over j with {i,j} ∈ E(G) of w_{ij} (p_j − p_i) = 0.
The set W(G, P) of all self-stresses is a real vector space, called the self-stress space at P.

Define an equivalence relation on B_d(G) as follows. Two realizations P and P' are equivalent if there is a sign-preserving homeomorphism between W(G, P) and W(G, P'); that is, a homeomorphism ϕ : W(G, P) → W(G, P') such that for every edge e ∈ E(G) and every w ∈ W(G, P), the sign of ϕ(w)(e) equals the sign of w(e) (with sign 0 preserved as 0). The equivalence classes form a stratification of B_d(G), and one records both the strata (organized by dimension) and the adjacency relations between strata (which strata lie in the closure of which).

Problem. Describe explicitly the combinatorial structure of these stratifications in the following three cases:
(a) G = K_6 and d = 2 (the complete graph on 6 vertices in the plane);
(b) G = K_4 and d = 3 (the complete graph on 4 vertices in 3-space);
(c) G = K_5 and d = 3 (the complete graph on 5 vertices in 3-space).
For each case, list all strata of every dimension and determine the adjacency relations among them.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of describing the combinatorial stratifications of B_2(K_6), B_3(K_4), and B_3(K_5) is posed as an open problem in the study of tensegrity configuration spaces. Stratifications for B_2(K_n) with small n (n ≤ 5) have been worked out, but the listed three cases remain unstudied; no published resolution of these specific cases was found.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
status_evidence.snippet: The next simplest and most interesting unstudied cases are B_2(K_6), B_3(K_4) and B_3(K_5).
status_evidence.claim: These three stratification problems are explicitly listed as open.
